issues.legal_issue: A purchaser who is unable or unwilling to make an essential part payment within the agreed or reasonable time is not entitled to specific performance of an immovable-property sale contract.
material_facts: The sale agreement required the purchaser to pay a substantial part of the price within five months, stated that time was of the essence, and provided that this payment was not earnest money.

The seller explained that she needed the payment to obtain alternative accommodation before delivering vacant possession and, after the payment deadline passed, gave the purchaser a further short period to pay.

The purchaser did not pay and stated that he could not raise the money unless the seller first made a separate agreement with a proposed cooperative housing society. The agreement did not make that separate agreement a condition precedent to payment.
The proposed society was never registered, and there was no evidence that the purchaser had the money or could pay within a reasonable time.

The trial court found that the purchaser was not ready and willing to perform the agreement, but the High Court granted specific performance. The purchaser also failed to make the payments required by the High Court's decree within its specified period.
issues.conclusion: The purchaser was not ready and willing to perform the agreement, and specific performance would be unfair and unreasonable. The High Court's decree was set aside and the trial court's dismissal of the suit was restored.
issues.legal_principle: A plaintiff seeking specific performance must be ready and willing to perform the plaintiff's part of the contract at all material times. Although time is not ordinarily of the essence in a contract for sale of immovable property, the parties' intention that performance occur within a reasonable time may be inferred from the express terms, the nature of the property, and the surrounding circumstances. The Court applied Chand Rani (Smt.) (Dead) by Lrs. v. Kamal Rani (Smt.) (Dead) by Lrs. (1993) 1 SCC 519, which considered those principles and readiness and willingness, and Parakunnan Veetill Joseph's Son Mathew v. Nedumbara Kuruvila's Son, (1987) Supp SCC 340, which requires careful consideration of the facts and circumstances so that specific performance is not used oppressively to secure an unfair advantage.

predicates.specific_performance_suit: A purchaser brought a suit seeking an order requiring the seller to complete a property sale.
predicates.immovable_property_sale_contract: The parties made a contract for the sale of immovable property.
predicates.substantial_part_payment_due_by_fixed_ti: The contract required the purchaser to make a substantial part payment by a specified time.
predicates.contract_or_circumstances_made_payment_t: The contract's terms and the circumstances surrounding performance made timely payment important to completion.
predicates.purchaser_unable_to_pay_within_reasonabl: The purchaser did not have, and was not shown to be able to obtain, the required payment within a reasonable time.
predicates.purchaser_conditioned_payment_on_unforme: The purchaser made payment dependent on a separate agreement with a proposed society that was never formed.
predicates.seller_needed_payment_for_alternative_ho: The seller needed the payment to obtain alternative accommodation in order to perform the obligation to deliver vacant possession.

issues.definition: When a purchaser seeking specific performance of an immovable-property sale was unable to make a time-critical substantial payment within a reasonable time, conditioned payment on an agreement with a society that was never formed, and the seller needed the payment for alternative housing, the purchaser is not granted specific performance.

issues.legal_issue: An appeal concerning an extension of time to pay under a conditional specific-performance decree becomes redundant when the underlying decree is set aside.
material_facts: The purchaser appealed the High Court's refusal to extend the time for payment required by its conditional specific-performance decree.
The Court set aside that decree in the related appeal, making the dispute about extending its payment deadline redundant.
The Court did not examine whether a court may extend time after passing such a conditional decree.
issues.conclusion: The appeal concerning extension of time was dismissed as redundant, without deciding whether the High Court had power to extend the time for payment.
issues.legal_principle: Where the decree imposing a payment deadline is set aside, an appeal solely concerning an extension of time to comply with that decree need not be examined because the dispute has become redundant.

predicates.appeal_from_refusal_to_extend_payment_ti: A party appealed an order refusing more time to make payment required by a decree.
predicates.underlying_conditional_decree_set_aside: The decree that imposed the payment requirement and deadline was set aside in a related proceeding.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns refusal to extend a payment deadline and the decree imposing that deadline has been set aside, the extension appeal is dismissed as redundant.
